Equipment inventory and organisation chart or headcount record evidencing adequate equipment and manpower

obligations.title: Ensure principal officer meets qualification, experience and NISM certification norms
obligations.summary: The principal officer must hold a professional qualification in finance, law, accountancy or business management (or a NISM Post Graduate Program in Securities Market of at least one year, or a CFA charter), have at least five years' securities-market experience of which at least two years are in portfolio management, investment advisory or fund management, and hold the relevant NISM certification. Portfolio managers registered before the 2020 Regulations had to meet the qualification and experience criteria within thirty-six months of commencement.

clause.excerpt: (d) the principal officer of the applicant has– [(i) a professional qualification in finance, law, accountancy or business management from a university or an institution recognized by the Central Government or any State Government or a foreign university or a professional qualification by completing a Post Graduate Program in the Securities Market (Portfolio Management) from NISM of a duration not less than one year or a professional qualification by obtaining a CFA charter from the CFA institute;] (ii) experience of at least five years in related activities in the securities market including in a portfolio manager, stock broker, investment advisor, research analyst or as a fund manager; and (iii) the relevant NISM certification as specified by the Board from time to time

control.name: Principal officer eligibility verification
control.description: On appointment and on any change of principal officer, verify the professional qualification, at least five years of securities-market experience including two years in portfolio management, investment advisory or fund management, and a valid NISM certification.

evidenceSpec.description: Principal officer's degree, CFA charter or NISM program certificate together with experience certificates evidencing five years in securities-market activities
Principal officer record shows the required qualification, five years' experience including two years in portfolio management or investment advisory or fund management, and a valid NISM certification

obligations.title: Employ at least one suitably qualified and experienced employee
obligations.summary: In addition to the principal officer and compliance officer, the firm must employ at least one person holding a recognised graduation and at least two years' experience in securities-market related activities. Firms registered before the 2020 Regulations had twelve months from commencement to meet this staffing requirement.

clause.excerpt: In addition to the Principal Officer and Compliance Officer, the applicant has in its employment at least one person with the following qualifications :- (i) graduation from a university or an institution recognized by the Central Government or any State Government or a foreign university; and (ii) an experience of at least two years in related activities in the securities market including in a portfolio manager, stock broker, investment advisor or as a fund manager

control.name: Minimum staffing qualification check
control.description: Maintain at least one employee, besides the principal officer and compliance officer, who holds a recognised graduation and at least two years of related securities-market experience, and track this headcount requirement on an ongoing basis.

evidenceSpec.description: Degree certificate and experience letters for the qualifying employee
HR record confirms at least one employee meeting the graduation and two-year experience criteria

obligations.title: Ensure fund-management decision makers meet principal officer criteria
obligations.summary: Any employee of the portfolio manager who has decision-making authority related to fund management must hold the same minimum qualifications, experience and certification as specified for the principal officer.

clause.excerpt: Provided that any employee of the Portfolio Manager who has decision making authority related to fund management shall have the same [minimum qualifications, experience and certification] as specified for the Principal Officer in clause (d) of sub- regulation (2) of regulation 7

control.name: Decision-authority mapping and qualification verification
control.description: Identify every employee with decision-making authority over fund management and verify that each holds the minimum qualifications, experience and NISM certification required of the principal officer; re-verify whenever such roles are assigned or changed.

evidenceSpec.description: Mapping of fund-management decision-making roles to personnel whose qualification, experience and certification records match principal officer requirements
Qualification and certification documents for each identified decision maker

obligations.title: Renew NISM certification before expiry of existing certification
obligations.summary: A fresh NISM certification must be obtained before the validity of the existing certification expires, so that compliance with the certification requirement is continuous.

clause.excerpt: Provided further that a fresh NISM certification shall be obtained before expiry of the validity of the existing certification to ensure continuity in compliance with the certification requirements

control.name: Certification expiry tracker
control.description: Track the validity dates of all NISM certifications held by the principal officer and other relevant personnel, and schedule and complete the fresh certification before each expiry date.

evidenceSpec.description: Fresh NISM certification obtained before expiry of the prior certification
Certification tracker shows no gap, with each new certification date preceding the previous certification's expiry date

obligations.title: Maintain net worth of at least five crore rupees
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must maintain net worth, as defined in the Explanation, of not less than five crore rupees. The Co-Investment Portfolio Manager is exempt from this requirement.

clause.excerpt: The net worth referred to in clause (g) of regulation 7 shall not be less than five crore rupees

control.name: Net worth threshold monitoring
control.description: Compute net worth as paid-up equity capital plus free reserves (excluding revaluation reserves) less accumulated losses and unwritten-off deferred expenditure, compare against the five crore rupee floor, and escalate and remediate any shortfall.

evidenceSpec.description: Net worth computation (paid-up equity capital plus free reserves excluding revaluation reserves, reduced by accumulated losses and unwritten-off deferred expenditure) showing a value of at least five crore rupees
Chartered accountant certificate or audited statement certifying net worth of not less than five crore rupees

obligations.title: Fulfill net worth requirements separately from capital adequacy for each activity
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must meet the net worth requirements under these regulations separately and independently of any capital adequacy requirements applicable to each activity it undertakes under other relevant regulations.

clause.excerpt: shall fulfill the net worth requirements under these regulations, separately and independently, of the capital adequacy requirements, if any, for each activity undertaken by it under the relevant regulations

control.name: Activity-wise segregation check
control.description: Compute and evidence net worth compliance separately from, and independently of, the capital adequacy maintained for each other regulated activity, with no cross-utilisation between the two requirements.

evidenceSpec.description: Activity-wise compliance report demonstrating that net worth requirements are met separately and independently of capital adequacy requirements for each regulated activity

obligations.title: Abide by the provisions of the Act and these regulations
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must conduct its business in compliance with the Act and the portfolio management regulations for as long as the registration remains valid.

clause.excerpt: the portfolio manager shall abide by the provisions of the Act and these regulations

control.name: Regulatory compliance framework
control.description: Maintain policies, monitoring and periodic compliance certification that map operations to the Act and the regulations, detect deviations and drive remediation.

evidenceSpec.description: Signed compliance attestation confirming adherence to the Act and the regulations
Register of identified regulatory deviations with remediation status

obligations.title: Obtain SEBI prior approval for change in control
obligations.summary: No change in control of the portfolio manager may take effect until prior approval of the Board has been obtained in the manner specified by it.

clause.excerpt: the portfolio manager shall obtain prior approval of the Board in case of change in control in such manner as may be specified by the Board

control.name: Change-in-control approval gate
control.description: Screening step in corporate transaction approvals ensuring any arrangement resulting in a change in control is not executed before SEBI's prior approval is secured and filed.

evidenceSpec.description: SEBI prior-approval letter for the change in control together with the related transaction documents

obligations.title: Inform SEBI forthwith of false information or material change
obligations.summary: If any information or particulars previously submitted to SEBI are found false or misleading in a material particular, or if there is any material change in the information already submitted, the portfolio manager must inform the Board in writing forthwith.

clause.excerpt: the portfolio manager shall forthwith inform the Board in writing, if any information or particulars previously submitted to the Board are found to be false or misleading in any material particular or if there is any material change in the information already submitted

control.name: Material-change disclosure trigger
control.description: Escalation workflow that reviews earlier filings for falsity or material change and, on detection, generates a written intimation to SEBI forthwith with dispatch proof.

evidenceSpec.description: Written intimation(s) to SEBI with dispatch date and the corrected or changed particulars
Log of detections of false, misleading or materially changed information and corresponding SEBI intimations

obligations.title: Redress grievances within 21 days and report complaints to SEBI
obligations.summary: Investor complaints must be redressed within 21 calendar days of receipt, and the portfolio manager must keep the Board informed of the number, nature and other particulars of complaints received.

clause.excerpt: the portfolio manager shall take adequate steps for redressal of grievances of the investors within [twenty-one calendar days] of the date of the receipt of the complaint and keep the Board informed about the number, nature and other particulars of the complaints received

control.name: Investor grievance redressal workflow
control.description: Complaint register tracking receipt and resolution dates so each complaint is closed within 21 calendar days, with complaint statistics (number, nature, particulars) compiled and filed with SEBI.

evidenceSpec.description: Complaint register showing date of receipt and date of redressal for each investor complaint
Complaint statistics (number, nature and particulars) reported to SEBI

obligations.title: Cease portfolio management activity while certificate is suspended
obligations.summary: If the Board suspends the portfolio manager's certificate for failure to pay fees under Schedule II, the portfolio manager must immediately stop carrying on portfolio management activity for the entire period the suspension remains in force.

clause.excerpt: the portfolio manager shall forthwith cease to carry on the activity as a portfolio manager for the period during which the suspension subsists.

control.name: Suspension cessation protocol
control.description: Upon receipt of notice that the Board has suspended the certificate, the firm immediately halts all portfolio management activity — no new mandates, no client transactions, no advisory or discretionary management — and maintains the halt until the suspension is lifted and formally communicated.

evidenceSpec.description: Activity report showing zero portfolio management transactions, new mandates, or client fee accruals from the suspension date until reinstatement.

obligations.title: Execute written client agreement before taking up a portfolio management assignment
obligations.summary: Before taking up an assignment to manage a client's funds and portfolio, the portfolio manager must enter into a written agreement with the client that defines the relationship and sets out mutual rights, liabilities and obligations, containing the details specified in Schedule IV.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall, before taking up an assignment of management of funds and portfolio on behalf of a client, enter into an agreement in writing with such client that clearly defines the inter se relationship and sets out their mutual rights, liabilities and obligations relating to management of portfolio containing the details as specified in Schedule IV

control.name: Client agreement gate
control.description: No client onboarding or assignment of funds is accepted until a written portfolio management agreement, containing all Schedule IV details and defining the mutual rights, liabilities and obligations, is executed and stored; the onboarding checklist blocks account activation without the signed agreement.

evidenceSpec.description: Executed written client agreements containing the Schedule IV details, on file for each client
Report mapping each client assignment commencement date to the execution date of the signed agreement, confirming the agreement predates taking up the assignment

obligations.title: Provide Disclosure Document and Form C certificate before agreement
obligations.summary: Prior to entering into an agreement with a client, the portfolio manager must provide the Disclosure Document in the format specified by the Board, together with a certificate in Form C as specified in Schedule I.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall provide to the client, the Disclosure Document, in the format as may be specified by the Board, along with a certificate in Form C as specified in Schedule I, prior to entering into an agreement with the client

control.name: Pre-agreement disclosure gate
control.description: Deliver the Board-format Disclosure Document along with the Form C certificate before signing the client agreement; the account-onboarding checklist gates agreement execution on confirmed delivery.

evidenceSpec.description: Dated delivery acknowledgement of the Disclosure Document and Form C certificate, timestamped before the signed client agreement

obligations.title: Disclose client fees for each service in the Disclosure Document
obligations.summary: The Disclosure Document must state the quantum and manner of payment of fees the client pays for each activity for which service is rendered by the portfolio manager, including services rendered indirectly through outsourcing.

clause.excerpt: (a) the quantum and manner of payment of fees payable by the client for each activity for which service is rendered by the portfolio manager directly or indirectly (where such service is out sourced)

control.name: Fee disclosure schedule review
control.description: Maintain a master fee schedule covering every activity for which service is rendered, directly or through outsourced providers; before each issue or update of the Disclosure Document, verify that the quantum and manner of payment of fees are stated for each such activity.

evidenceSpec.description: Current Disclosure Document fee section showing quantum and manner of payment for each activity, including outsourced services

obligations.title: Disclose portfolio risks for each investment approach
obligations.summary: The Disclosure Document must disclose portfolio risks, including risks specific to each investment approach offered by the portfolio manager.

clause.excerpt: (b) portfolio risks including risk specific to each investment approach offered by the portfolio manager

control.name: Investment-approach risk mapping
control.description: Maintain risk disclosures mapped to each investment approach offered; review whenever an approach is added, modified or discontinued so the Disclosure Document always states portfolio risks including approach-specific risks.

evidenceSpec.description: Disclosure Document risk section listing portfolio risks and risks specific to every investment approach offered

obligations.title: Disclose related-party transactions and conflicts of interest
obligations.summary: The Disclosure Document must contain complete disclosures of transactions with related parties as per the accounting standards specified by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India, and details of conflicts of interest related to services offered by the portfolio manager's group companies or associates.

clause.excerpt: (c) complete disclosures of transactions with related parties as per the accounting standards specified by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India; (d) details of conflicts of interest related to services offered by group companies or associates of the portfolio manager

control.name: Related-party and conflict register
control.description: Maintain a register of transactions with related parties classified per ICAI-specified accounting standards and of conflicts of interest arising from services offered by group companies or associates; reconcile the register into the Disclosure Document at each issue or update.

evidenceSpec.description: Disclosure Document section containing related-party transaction disclosures and group-company conflict of interest details
Related-party transaction register reconciled to the transactions and counterparties disclosed in the Disclosure Document

obligations.title: Disclose performance with prescribed return methodology
obligations.summary: The Disclosure Document must disclose the performance of the portfolio manager; for a discretionary portfolio manager, performance must be calculated using Time Weighted Rate of Return for the immediately preceding three years and performance indicators must also be disclosed. A Co-investment Portfolio Manager's performance is calculated as agreed with the client.

clause.excerpt: (e) the performance of the portfolio manager: Provided that the performance of a discretionary portfolio manager shall be calculated using ‘Time Weighted Rate of Return’ for the immediately preceding three years

control.name: Performance computation and disclosure control
control.description: Compute performance using Time Weighted Rate of Return over the immediately preceding three years for discretionary portfolios, calculate and disclose the applicable performance indicators, and include the results in the Disclosure Document; for co-investment mandates, compute performance as agreed with the client.

evidenceSpec.description: Disclosure Document performance section showing three-year Time Weighted Rate of Return figures and disclosed performance indicators for discretionary portfolios

obligations.title: Disclose audited financial statements of preceding three years
obligations.summary: The Disclosure Document must include the audited financial statements of the portfolio manager for the immediately preceding three years.

clause.excerpt: (f) the audited financial statements of the portfolio manager for the immediately preceding three years.

control.name: Audited financials inclusion check
control.description: Before each issue or update of the Disclosure Document, confirm that the audited financial statements covering the immediately preceding three financial years are appended or incorporated in the document.

evidenceSpec.description: Audited financial statements for the preceding three years as included in the Disclosure Document, together with the auditor's report

obligations.title: Certify Disclosure Document contents via independent chartered accountant
obligations.summary: The contents of the Disclosure Document must be certified by an independent chartered accountant before it is used.

clause.excerpt: The contents of the Disclosure Document shall be certified by an independent chartered accountant.

control.name: Independent CA certification of Disclosure Document
control.description: Route the completed Disclosure Document to a chartered accountant with no role in its preparation or in the firm's operations, obtain their review and signed certification of its contents, and retain the certificate before the Disclosure Document is issued or used.

evidenceSpec.description: Signed certification statement from the independent chartered accountant covering the contents of the Disclosure Document, retained on file.

obligations.title: Keep Disclosure Document available on the portfolio manager's website at all times
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must ensure a copy of the Disclosure Document is accessible on its own website continuously and publish it as soon as registration is granted. Co-investment Portfolio Managers are exempt from this requirement.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall ensure that a copy of Disclosure Document is available on the website of the portfolio manager at all times and as soon as the registration is granted

control.name: Website Disclosure Document availability monitoring
control.description: Maintain a hosting process that publishes the Disclosure Document on the portfolio manager's website immediately upon grant of registration, and operate an automated uptime/content check that alerts if the document becomes unavailable so it can be restored without interruption.

evidenceSpec.description: Automated website scan of the portfolio manager's public URL confirming the Disclosure Document is present, downloadable, and continuously available, with scan results logged over time.
Record of registration grant and the timestamp showing the Disclosure Document was first published on the website as soon as registration was granted.

obligations.title: File disclosure document with Board within 7 working days of any material change
obligations.summary: Whenever a material change, including a change in the investment approach, is effected, the portfolio manager must file the disclosure document together with the material change with the Board within 7 working days from the date of the change.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall file the disclosure document with the material change within 7 working days from the date of the change.

control.name: Material change disclosure filing workflow
control.description: A register of material changes (including changes in the investment approach) recording the date each change is effected, which triggers preparation and filing of the updated disclosure document with the Board within 7 working days of that date.

evidenceSpec.description: Change register recording each material change date and the corresponding filing date, demonstrating submission within 7 working days
Updated disclosure document as filed with the Board for each material change, with submission acknowledgement

obligations.title: File disclosure document with certificate in Form C
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must file the disclosure document together with the certificate in Form C as specified in Schedule I.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall file disclosure document along with the certificate in Form C as specified in Schedule I.

control.name: Disclosure document filing control
control.description: Maintain a process to prepare the disclosure document, obtain the certificate in Form C as specified in Schedule I, and file both documents together, logging the filing date and acknowledgement.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the filed disclosure document along with the certificate in Form C as specified in Schedule I, with filing acknowledgement

obligations.title: Disclose change in Principal Officer identity to Board and clients within 7 working days
obligations.summary: When the identity of the Principal Officer changes, the portfolio manager must notify the Board (SEBI) and its clients of the change. The notification must be made within 7 working days of the change taking effect.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall disclose a change in the identity of the Principal Officer to the Board and the clients within 7 working days of effecting the change.

control.name: Principal Officer change notification
control.description: Maintain a process that detects any change in the identity of the Principal Officer, triggers preparation of a disclosure to SEBI (the Board) and to all clients, and ensures the disclosure is dispatched within 7 working days of the change taking effect, with the change and notification dates logged for tracking.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the disclosure communication sent to the Board (SEBI) and to clients announcing the change in Principal Officer identity, showing the date of the change and the date of dispatch
Register of Principal Officer changes recording the effective date of each change and the notification date, confirming the interval does not exceed 7 working days

obligations.title: Uniform reporting of performance across all channels
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must present its performance on a uniform basis in disclosures to the Board, marketing materials, reports to its clients and on its website.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall report its performance uniformly in the disclosures to the Board, marketing materials and reports to the clients and on its website.

control.name: Uniform performance disclosure control
control.description: Maintain a single master performance dataset and run a reconciliation step before publication to ensure the same performance figures and methodology appear in Board disclosures, marketing materials, client reports and website content.

evidenceSpec.description: Version-controlled master performance disclosure showing the identical performance figures used in Board disclosures, marketing materials, client reports and website updates
Cross-channel reconciliation report comparing performance figures across the four channels and flagging any mismatch

obligations.title: Disclose range of fees charged under various heads in the disclosure document
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must disclose, in the disclosure document, the range of fees charged under each of the various fee heads.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall disclose the range of fees charged under various heads in the disclosure document.

control.name: Fee range disclosure control
control.description: Maintain the disclosure document so that it lists the range of fees charged under every fee head, and update it whenever the fee structure changes.

evidenceSpec.description: The current disclosure document showing the range of fees charged under various heads

obligations.title: Submit investor claims and disputes to Board-specified dispute resolution mechanism
obligations.summary: All claims, differences or disputes between investors and the portfolio manager arising from the portfolio manager's securities market activities must be submitted to a dispute resolution mechanism that includes mediation and/or conciliation and/or arbitration, following the procedure specified by the Board.

clause.excerpt: All claims, differences or disputes between investors and the portfolio manager arising out of or in relation to the activities of the portfolio manager in the securities market shall be submitted to a dispute resolution mechanism that includes mediation and/or conciliation and/or arbitration, in accordance with the procedure specified by the Board.

control.name: Investor dispute escalation to mediation, conciliation or arbitration
control.description: Maintain a documented dispute resolution procedure under which every investor claim, difference or dispute arising from the portfolio manager's securities market activities is logged and referred to mediation and/or conciliation and/or arbitration in line with the Board-specified procedure, with status and outcome tracked for each case.

evidenceSpec.description: Dispute resolution procedure document mapping each dispute category to mediation, conciliation and/or arbitration steps as specified by the Board
Register of investor claims and disputes showing referral date, mechanism used (mediation, conciliation or arbitration) and outcome, confirming each was submitted to the mechanism

obligations.title: Discretionary PM to manage each client's funds individually, not as a Mutual Fund
obligations.summary: A discretionary portfolio manager must manage the funds of each client individually and independently in line with that client's needs, in a manner that does not take on the character of a Mutual Fund.

clause.excerpt: The discretionary portfolio manager shall individually and independently manage the funds of each client in accordance with the needs of the client, in a manner which does not partake character of a Mutual Fund

control.name: Client-wise segregated portfolio management
control.description: Maintain separate client-level accounts and independent investment decisioning so every discretionary client's funds are managed to that client's own needs, with periodic checks that portfolio structure and pooling do not replicate a Mutual Fund.

evidenceSpec.description: Client-wise portfolio and account records demonstrating individual, independent management of each client's funds
Periodic compliance attestation that discretionary portfolios do not partake the character of a Mutual Fund

obligations.title: Do not accept client funds or securities worth less than fifty lakh rupees
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must not accept funds or securities from a client valued below fifty lakh rupees. The minimum applies to new clients and fresh investments by existing clients, while accredited investors, the Co-investment Portfolio Manager, and investments existing as on the notification date are outside the requirement.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall not accept from the client, funds or securities worth less than fifty lakh rupees

control.name: Minimum investment amount gate
control.description: Before accepting any funds or securities from a client — for new clients and for each fresh investment by an existing client — verify that the value is at least fifty lakh rupees, and reject or return any amount below that threshold, recording the check performed for each acceptance.

evidenceSpec.description: Data check over client acceptance records confirming every accepted investment from new clients and fresh investments by existing clients meets the fifty lakh rupee minimum, with below-threshold amounts rejected or returned.
Client onboarding and investment acceptance files evidencing that the minimum investment amount was verified before funds or securities were accepted.

obligations.title: Act in a fiduciary capacity with regard to client's funds
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must handle client funds in a fiduciary capacity, placing the client's interest first at all times when managing or dealing with those funds.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall act in a fiduciary capacity with regard to the client's funds.

control.name: Fiduciary duty conduct standard
control.description: Maintain and enforce a firm-wide fiduciary conduct standard covering all handling of client funds: decisions and transactions on client funds must prioritise the client's interest, conflicts of interest must be identified and managed or disclosed, and client funds must not be used for any benefit of the portfolio manager contrary to the client's interest. All staff dealing with client funds are trained and bound by this standard.

evidenceSpec.description: Written fiduciary conduct policy covering custody, use and deployment of client funds, including conflict-of-interest identification and disclosure procedures, approved by senior management.
Periodic attestation or review record confirming that all client fund transactions were executed in the client's interest, with any identified conflicts logged and resolved or disclosed.

obligations.title: Maintain client funds in a separate account with a Scheduled Commercial Bank
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must keep the funds of all clients in a separate account maintained with a Scheduled Commercial Bank, meaning a bank included in the Second Schedule to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall keep the funds of all clients in a separate account to be maintained by it in a Scheduled Commercial Bank.

control.name: Segregated client funds bank account control
control.description: Operate a dedicated bank account for all client funds at a bank included in the Second Schedule to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and verify on an ongoing basis that the account is separate from the portfolio manager's own accounts and that no client funds are held elsewhere.

evidenceSpec.description: Bank confirmation letter and account statement evidencing a separate client funds account maintained with a bank in the Second Schedule to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
Reconciliation confirming all client funds are held in the designated separate Scheduled Commercial Bank account with no commingling of the portfolio manager's own funds

obligations.title: Transact within client-placed dealing limitations
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must carry out securities transactions only within the limitations that the client has itself placed on dealing in securities under the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall transact in securities within the limitation placed by the client himself with regard to dealing in securities under the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934).

control.name: Client mandate limit check
control.description: Record each client's dealing limitations stipulated under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 in the portfolio management system and test every order against those limits before execution, blocking or escalating any transaction that would breach them.

evidenceSpec.description: Client agreement or written instruction capturing the client's limitations on dealing in securities under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
Pre-trade compliance log evidencing that each transaction was tested against the client's stated dealing limitations with no breaches.

obligations.title: Prohibition on borrowing funds or securities on behalf of clients
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must not borrow funds or securities on behalf of any client.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall not borrow funds or securities on behalf of the client.

control.name: Client borrowing prohibition control
control.description: Maintain policies and system checks that prevent any borrowing of funds or securities on behalf of clients, including account-level monitoring and pre-trade checks to detect and block any borrowing arranged for a client's account.

evidenceSpec.description: Query or exception report over client accounts and funding arrangements showing no funds or securities borrowed on behalf of clients
Internal compliance certificate or policy document attesting that no client borrowings were effected during the review period

obligations.title: Do not lend client securities to third persons
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager is prohibited from lending securities held on behalf of its clients to any third person, except where permitted under the regulations.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall not lend securities held on behalf of the clients to a third person except as provided under these regulations.

control.name: Client securities lending prohibition control
control.description: The firm maintains a policy and system control that blocks or holds any transfer, pledge or lending of securities from client accounts to third parties unless the transaction is verified as falling within an exception expressly permitted under the regulations, with compliance sign-off on each such exception.

evidenceSpec.description: Internal policy (e.g., board-approved operating policy) recording the prohibition on lending client-held securities and the narrow regulatory exceptions, with approval workflow for any permitted lending.
Periodic reconciliation of debits, pledges and outward transfers from client securities accounts against the list of permitted exceptions to confirm no unauthorised lending occurred.
Automated surveillance of securities movement instructions out of client accounts that flags any lending or transfer to a third person for review before execution.

obligations.title: Ensure distributors comply with PMS regulations and circulars
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must ensure that every person or entity distributing its services carries out those distribution activities in compliance with the PMS regulations and the circulars issued thereunder from time to time.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall ensure that any person or entity involved in the distribution of its services is carrying out the distribution activities in compliance with these regulations and circulars issued thereunder from time to time.

control.name: Distributor compliance oversight
control.description: Maintain a register of all distributors, periodically review their distribution activities against the PMS regulations and SEBI circulars, obtain compliance confirmations from them, and take corrective action where deviations are found.

evidenceSpec.description: Distributor oversight review records and compliance confirmations obtained from each distributor
Register of distributors mapped to latest compliance review dates with no distributor overdue for review

obligations.title: Ensure compliance with the Investor Charter specified by the Board
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must comply with the Investor Charter specified by SEBI from time to time, adopting each updated version as it is issued.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall ensure compliance with the Investor Charter specified by the Board from time to time.

control.name: Investor Charter compliance monitoring
control.description: Track updates to the Investor Charter issued by SEBI, operationalise its service standards within the firm, and periodically verify that client-facing practices conform to the Charter.

evidenceSpec.description: Investor Charter adopted by the firm and records of updates as re-specified by the Board
Client-facing disclosures and service processes checked against the current Investor Charter

obligations.title: Invest or manage client money/securities only per the client agreement
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must not invest or manage any money or securities accepted from a client except in accordance with the terms of the agreement between the portfolio manager and that client.

clause.excerpt: The money or securities accepted by the portfolio manager shall not be invested or managed by the portfolio manager except in terms of the agreement between the portfolio manager and the client.

control.name: Mandate-conformance check
control.description: Before executing any investment or management action on client assets, verify the action falls within the investment mandate and terms of the signed portfolio management agreement for that specific client; block or escalate any action outside the agreement.

evidenceSpec.description: Client-level log mapping each investment and management action to the corresponding signed portfolio management agreement, with exceptions flagged and resolved.

obligations.title: Treat renewal of matured portfolio as a fresh placement
obligations.summary: When a portfolio is renewed upon maturity of its initial period, the renewal must be processed and documented as a fresh placement rather than a continuation. The proviso exempts the Co-investment Portfolio Manager from this requirement.

clause.excerpt: Any renewal of portfolio on maturity of the initial period shall be deemed as a fresh placement

control.name: Renewal onboarding as fresh placement
control.description: When a client portfolio reaches the end of its initial period and the client elects to renew, route the renewal through the same onboarding workflow used for new placements, including a fresh agreement and placement documentation, instead of rolling it over as a continuation.

evidenceSpec.description: Renewal records for matured portfolios showing fresh placement processing and newly executed client agreements for each renewal.

obligations.title: Permit withdrawal of client funds or securities before maturity on trigger events
obligations.summary: Notwithstanding the terms of the portfolio management agreement referred to in regulation 22, the client may withdraw funds or securities before the contract matures when portfolio management services are terminated, the portfolio manager's registration is suspended or cancelled by the Board, or the portfolio manager enters bankruptcy or liquidation. The termination-based trigger does not apply in the case of a Co-investment Portfolio Manager.

clause.excerpt: the funds or securities can be withdrawn by the client before the maturity of the contract under the following circumstances, namely- (a) voluntary or compulsory termination of portfolio management services by the portfolio manager or the client

control.name: Premature withdrawal event handling
control.description: Monitor for the occurrence of the specified trigger events - termination of portfolio management services by either party, suspension or cancellation of the SEBI certificate of registration, or bankruptcy or liquidation of the portfolio manager. Upon any such event, permit the client to withdraw funds and securities before contract maturity irrespective of any contrary term in the portfolio management agreement, applying the termination trigger only to non-co-investment portfolios.

evidenceSpec.description: Client withdrawal requests together with release and settlement records evidencing return of funds or securities on occurrence of a trigger event
Register of trigger events (termination notices, Board orders of suspension or cancellation, bankruptcy or liquidation filings) reconciled against completed client withdrawals
Copies of supporting trigger documentation such as termination letters, SEBI suspension or cancellation orders, or insolvency and liquidation records retained for each premature withdrawal

obligations.title: Invest discretionary client funds only in permitted securities
obligations.summary: A discretionary portfolio manager must invest client funds only in securities listed or traded on a recognized stock exchange, money market instruments, units of Mutual Funds, and other securities specified by the Board.

clause.excerpt: The discretionary portfolio manager shall invest funds of his clients in the securities listed or traded on a recognized stock exchange, money market instruments, units of Mutual Funds and other securities as specified by Board from time to time, on behalf of their clients.

control.name: Permitted investment universe check
control.description: Before executing any discretionary client trade, verify the instrument falls within the approved universe: exchange-listed/traded securities, money market instruments, Mutual Fund units, or Board-specified securities; block anything outside the list.

evidenceSpec.description: Written investment universe policy listing the permitted instrument classes for discretionary portfolios
Mapping of client portfolio holdings to the permitted instrument classes showing no out-of-universe positions

obligations.title: Put in place an alert-based system for prudential limit compliance
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must implement an alert-based system that monitors compliance with the prudential limits on investments.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall put in place an alert based system to monitor compliance with the prudential limits on investments.

control.name: Alert-based limit monitoring system
control.description: Configure a monitoring system that automatically generates alerts when client-level investments approach or breach the prudential limits, with defined escalation and resolution procedures for triggered alerts.

evidenceSpec.description: System configuration document showing alert rules, thresholds tied to the prudential limits, and escalation workflow
Demonstration of the running alert system generating alerts on limit approach or breach for client portfolios

obligations.title: No distribution related fees on direct plan Mutual Fund investments
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must not charge the client any kind of distribution related fee when investing in units of Mutual Funds through the direct plan.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager while investing in units of Mutual Funds through direct plan shall not charge any kind of distribution related fees to the client.

control.name: Direct plan fee prohibition check
control.description: A billing control that screens all client fee charges and blocks or reverses any distribution related fee levied in connection with investments in Mutual Fund direct plans, ensuring clients are never invoiced such fees.

evidenceSpec.description: Report of client invoices and billing records for the review period showing zero distribution related fees charged on direct plan Mutual Fund investments.
Internal fee schedule and client billing policy stating that no distribution related fees are charged on direct plan investments.

obligations.title: Prohibition on deploying clients' funds in bill discounting, badla financing or lending
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must not deploy clients' funds in bill discounting, badla financing, or for lending or placement with corporate or non-corporate bodies.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall not deploy the clients' funds in bill discounting, badla financing or for the purpose of lending or placement with corporate or non-corporate bodies.

control.name: Prohibited deployment screen
control.description: Every use of client funds is screened against a prohibited-avenue list covering bill discounting, badla financing, lending and placements with corporate or non-corporate bodies; blocked deployments are logged and escalated to compliance.

evidenceSpec.description: Exception report from the fund-deployment or order-management system evidencing zero client-fund deployments coded to bill discounting, badla financing, lending or placement counterparties
Compliance certificate signed by the compliance officer confirming no client funds were deployed in the prohibited avenues

obligations.title: No investing of client funds in portfolios of another portfolio manager
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager is prohibited from deploying clients' funds into any portfolio that is managed or administered by another portfolio manager. This restriction applies at all times to every investment made on behalf of clients.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall not invest the clients’ funds in the portfolio managed or administered by another portfolio manager.

control.name: Prohibited-investment pre-trade block
control.description: Configure the order management and investment process with a hard restriction that rejects any allocation of client funds into schemes or portfolios managed or administered by another portfolio manager, and review any blocked or attempted transactions for compliance sign-off.

evidenceSpec.description: Exception/attestation report from the investment system confirming that no client funds were invested in portfolios managed or administered by another portfolio manager during the review period
Investment policy or restricted-investment list documenting the prohibition on investing client funds with other portfolio managers, approved and acknowledged by compliance

obligations.title: Do not invest client funds based on advice of any other entity
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must form investment decisions for client funds independently and must not base any investment of client funds on advice received from any other entity.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall not invest client’s fund based on the advice of any other entity.

control.name: Independent investment decision control
control.description: Operate an in-house investment decision-making process that documents the internal rationale for each client investment, with a pre-trade check confirming the decision did not rely on advice from any external entity.

evidenceSpec.description: Investment decision records for client funds showing internal research and rationale, evidencing no reliance on any other entity's advice.
Review of trade rationale logs and correspondence to confirm no client investment was executed on the advice of another entity.

obligations.title: No speculative transactions while dealing with clients' funds
obligations.summary: Portfolio managers must not, while dealing with clients' funds, enter into any purchase or sale of a security that is settled otherwise than by actual delivery or transfer of the security; transactions in derivatives are the only permitted exception.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall not while dealing with clients’ funds indulge in speculative transactions i.e, it shall not enter into any transaction for purchase or sale of any security which is periodically or ultimately settled otherwise than by actual delivery or transfer of security except the transactions in derivatives.

control.name: Pre-trade non-delivery settlement blocker
control.description: A pre-trade compliance control that blocks any order in clients' funds for a security transaction that would be settled otherwise than by actual delivery or transfer of the security, while maintaining an exception whitelist permitting derivatives transactions. Supported by a post-trade settlement-mode reconciliation of all client trades.

evidenceSpec.description: Pre-trade screening log showing that all client-fund orders passed the non-delivery settlement check, with derivatives orders identified as the permitted exception.
Trade-level report reconciling every client securities transaction against its settlement mode, confirming settlement by actual delivery or transfer of securities except flagged derivatives trades.
Written internal policy (and client agreement clause) prohibiting speculative transactions in clients' funds, documenting the derivatives exception.

obligations.title: Allocate aggregated trades pro rata at weighted average price
obligations.summary: When the portfolio manager aggregates purchases or sales of securities across clients for economy of scale, the inter se allocation between clients must be done on a pro rata basis at the weighted average price of the day's transactions.

clause.excerpt: inter se allocation shall be done on a pro rata basis and at weighted average price of the day's transactions

control.name: Pro rata allocation engine check
control.description: For every aggregated order, compute each client's allocated quantity pro rata to participation and assign the weighted average price of the day's transactions; review allocation records before booking trades to client accounts.

evidenceSpec.description: Daily allocation report showing each client's allocated quantity, pro rata ratio and price equal to the weighted average price of the day's transactions

obligations.title: Close all trade allocations same day, keep no open positions
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must complete allocation of all sales and purchases effected in a day so that no open position remains in respect of that allocation.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall not keep any open position in respect of allocation of sales or purchases effected in a day

control.name: End-of-day allocation closure review
control.description: Run an end-of-day reconciliation of executed trades versus client allocations; any residual unallocated quantity is resolved the same day so that no open allocation position carries forward.

evidenceSpec.description: End-of-day reconciliation report evidencing zero open allocation positions for the day's purchases and sales

obligations.title: No off-market transfers in client accounts except in permitted circumstances
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager is prohibited from executing off-market transfers in a client's account unless the transfer falls within the stated exceptions, such as settlement of the client's own trades, providing margin/collateral for the client's own positions, dealing in unlisted securities per regulations, transfers with the client's specific consent for each transaction, or reasons specified by the Board.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall not execute off market transfers in client’s account except: (a) for settlement of the clients’ own trades; (b) for providing margin/ collateral for clients’ own positions; (c) for dealing in unlisted securities in accordance with the regulations; (d) with specific consent of the client for each transaction; (e) for any other reason specified by the Board from time to time.

control.name: Off-market transfer restriction with permitted-purpose whitelist
control.description: Block off-market transfer instructions in client accounts unless they map to an approved purpose (settlement of the client's own trades, margin/collateral for the client's own positions, unlisted securities dealings, Board-specified reasons) or carry documented specific client consent for that transaction; route any other off-market transfer request to compliance for rejection or review.

evidenceSpec.description: Reconciliation of off-market transfer logs against the permitted-purpose whitelist, flagging transfers outside the allowed grounds or lacking per-transaction client consent.
Client consent records evidencing specific consent obtained for each off-market transfer executed under the consent exception.

obligations.title: No client securities held in portfolio manager's own name
obligations.summary: A portfolio manager must not hold securities belonging to client portfolio accounts in its own name on behalf of clients, whether by virtue of a contract with clients or otherwise.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall not hold the securities belonging to the portfolio account, in its own name on behalf of its clients either by virtue of contract with clients or otherwise.

control.name: Own-name holdings check
control.description: Reconcile securities held in the portfolio manager's own demat/registry accounts against client portfolio account holdings to confirm no client securities are titled in the manager's own name, and transfer any such holdings out of the manager's name.

evidenceSpec.description: Reconciliation report matching securities registered in the portfolio manager's own name against client portfolio account holdings, showing zero matches.
Demat account statements evidencing that client portfolio securities are held in the clients' names and not in the portfolio manager's own name.

obligations.title: Keep and maintain prescribed books of accounts, records and documents
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must keep and maintain copies of the balance sheet, profit and loss account and auditor's report for each accounting period, together with a statement of financial position.

clause.excerpt: Every portfolio manager shall keep and maintain the following books of accounts, records and documents namely: - (a) a copy of balance sheet at the end of each accounting period; (b) a copy of the profit and loss account for each accounting period; (c) a copy of the auditor’s report on the accounts for each accounting period; (d) a statement of financial position and;

control.name: Statutory books and records repository
control.description: Maintain a repository holding a copy of the balance sheet, profit and loss account and auditor's report for each accounting period plus a statement of financial position, filing each document as the accounting period closes.

evidenceSpec.description: Copies of the balance sheet, profit and loss account and auditor's report for the latest completed accounting period, together with the statement of financial position, held on file

obligations.title: Record data, facts and opinion behind every investment decision under Principal Officer
obligations.summary: For every investment transaction or recommendation the portfolio manager must keep a record of the data, facts and opinion that led to the decision, and that record must be maintained under the hand of the Principal Officer.

clause.excerpt: (e) records in support of every investment transaction or recommendation which will indicate the data, facts and opinion leading to that investment decision: Provided that such a record shall be maintained under the hands of the Principal Officer of the portfolio manager.

control.name: Investment decision rationale record
control.description: For each investment transaction or recommendation, document the data, facts and analysis forming the basis of the decision and have the record maintained under the hand of the Principal Officer.

evidenceSpec.description: Rationale record for a sampled investment transaction or recommendation showing the underlying data, facts and opinion and bearing the Principal Officer's signature
Reconcile the investment transaction log against the rationale record register to confirm every transaction or recommendation has a linked record

obligations.title: Intimate SEBI the place where books and records are kept
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must inform the Board of the location where its books of accounts, records and documents are maintained.

clause.excerpt: Every portfolio manager shall intimate to the Board the place where the books of accounts, records and documents are maintained.

control.name: Records location intimation to SEBI
control.description: The firm identifies the premises where its books of accounts, records and documents are maintained and files a written intimation of that place with the Board, retaining proof of submission.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the intimation letter or email sent to SEBI stating the place where books of accounts, records and documents are maintained
SEBI acknowledgment or filing receipt evidencing receipt of the intimation

obligations.title: Furnish balance sheet and P&L account to the Board after each accounting period
obligations.summary: After each accounting period closes, the portfolio manager must send the Board copies of its balance sheet and profit and loss account.

clause.excerpt: every portfolio manager shall, after the end of each accounting period, furnish to the Board copies of the balance sheet, profit and loss account

control.name: Periodic financial statement filing
control.description: When each accounting period ends, compile the balance sheet and profit and loss account, obtain sign-off, submit copies to the Board, and log the submission date and acknowledgement received.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the balance sheet and profit and loss account submitted to the Board, with submission acknowledgement or dispatch proof
Filing log showing submission made after the close of each accounting period

obligations.title: Furnish other documents for preceding five accounting years when the Board requires
obligations.summary: On the Board's requisition, the portfolio manager must furnish such other documents covering the preceding five accounting years.

clause.excerpt: such other documents for the preceding five accounting years as and when required by the Board

control.name: Board-request document retrieval
control.description: Maintain an indexed archive of financial records for the preceding five accounting years so that any additional documents the Board calls for can be located, assembled and furnished promptly upon requisition.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the Board's requisition together with the documents furnished in response
Request log recording the requisition date, the documents supplied and the five-year coverage of the archive

obligations.title: Furnish net worth certificate issued by a chartered accountant to the Board when required
obligations.summary: Every portfolio manager must furnish to the Board a net worth certificate issued by a chartered accountant whenever the Board requires it.

clause.excerpt: Every portfolio manager shall furnish to the Board a net worth certificate issued by a chartered accountant as and when required by the Board.

control.name: Net worth certification and Board submission control
control.description: Maintain an arrangement with a chartered accountant to obtain a net worth certificate, and a tracking mechanism to detect any Board requisition and furnish the certificate to the Board promptly upon such requirement.

evidenceSpec.description: Net worth certificate issued by the chartered accountant as furnished to the Board.
Record of the Board's requisition and proof of submission of the certificate to the Board (e.g. filing acknowledgement or correspondence).

obligations.title: Annual audit of books of account by qualified auditor
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must get its books of account audited yearly by a qualified auditor to confirm proper accounting methods and procedures were followed and duties were performed in accordance with the law.

clause.excerpt: The books of account will be audited yearly by qualified auditor to ensure that the portfolio manager has followed proper accounting methods and procedures

control.name: Annual statutory audit of books of account
control.description: Engage a qualified auditor each accounting year to audit the books of account, verifying that accounting methods and procedures are proper and that the portfolio manager's duties were performed in accordance with the law, and retain the signed audit report.

evidenceSpec.description: Signed audit report on the books of account issued by the qualified auditor for the accounting year.

obligations.title: Submit audit certificate to the Board within six months of period close
obligations.summary: Where the Board so specifies, the portfolio manager must submit a certificate to the Board certifying that the yearly audit confirmed proper accounting methods and lawful performance of duties, within six months of the close of its accounting period.

clause.excerpt: A certificate to this effect shall, if so specified, be submitted to the Board within six months of close of portfolio manager's accounting period.

control.name: Certificate submission to the Board
control.description: On specification by the Board, prepare the certificate covering the audit findings on accounting methods and legal compliance, and submit it to the Board within six months of the close of the accounting period, logging the submission date and acknowledgement.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the certificate submitted to the Board together with proof of submission (acknowledgement or submission log entry).

obligations.title: Provide detailed statement of accounts to client on contract termination
obligations.summary: When the portfolio management contract is terminated, the portfolio manager must give the client a detailed statement of accounts.

clause.excerpt: On termination of the contract, the portfolio manager shall give a detailed statement of accounts to the client

control.name: Termination account statement issuance
control.description: Upon termination of a portfolio management contract, trigger a workflow that compiles a detailed statement of the client's accounts (transactions, holdings, fees, and balances) and delivers it to the client, with delivery logged against the termination event.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the detailed statement of accounts issued to the client on termination
Termination log mapping each terminated contract to the date the statement of accounts was delivered to the client

obligations.title: Settle the client's account as agreed in the contract on termination
obligations.summary: On termination of the contract, the portfolio manager must settle the account with the client in accordance with the terms agreed in the contract.

clause.excerpt: settle the account with the client as agreed in the contract

control.name: Post-termination account settlement
control.description: Upon contract termination, compute the final dues (funds and/or securities payable to or by the client) per the contract's agreed settlement terms, execute the settlement, and record confirmation of full settlement for each terminated account.

evidenceSpec.description: Settlement confirmation or client acknowledgment evidencing the account was settled as per the contract
Reconciliation report showing each terminated contract with a completed settlement matching contractually agreed terms

obligations.title: Provide client with details of his portfolio on request
obligations.summary: A client is entitled to obtain details of his portfolio from the portfolio manager, so the manager must furnish such portfolio details whenever the client requests them.

clause.excerpt: The client shall have the right to obtain details of his portfolio from the portfolio managers.

control.name: Client portfolio-detail request handling
control.description: Operate a channel through which clients can request details of their portfolio, capture each incoming request, compile the details of that client's portfolio as managed, and furnish them to the client, logging what was provided and when.

evidenceSpec.description: Portfolio details or statements furnished to clients in response to their requests, together with the corresponding request records
Register of client portfolio-detail requests matched against the responses sent and the dates of each

obligations.title: Rectify deficiencies in auditor's report within two months
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must take steps to rectify the deficiencies identified in the auditor's report under Regulation 30(2) within two months from the date of that report.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall take steps to rectify the deficiencies made out in the auditor’s report within two months from the date of the auditor’s report as specified in sub-regulation (2) of Regulation 30.

control.name: Auditor deficiency rectification tracking
control.description: On receipt of the auditor's report under Regulation 30(2), log each deficiency into a remediation tracker, assign owners and remediation actions, and drive each deficiency to closure within two months of the report date, recording evidence of the corrective steps taken.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the auditor's report under Regulation 30(2) with its date, establishing the start of the two-month rectification window.
Action-taken report or remediation log mapping each deficiency in the auditor's report to the corrective steps completed within two months.
Compliance tracker check that every deficiency from the auditor's report has a closure date no later than two months from the auditor's report date.

obligations.title: Compliance officer to report non-compliance immediately to Board
obligations.summary: The compliance officer must immediately and independently report to the Board any non-compliance that he observes.

clause.excerpt: The compliance officer shall immediately and independently report to the Board any non- compliance observed by him.

control.name: Compliance officer Board reporting of non-compliance
control.description: The compliance officer independently monitors for non-compliance and, upon observing any instance, escalates it directly to the Board without delay, maintaining a record of each escalation.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the compliance officer's report of the observed non-compliance submitted to the Board, with date of submission evidencing immediacy
Register of non-compliance observations cross-checked against Board reports to confirm every observed instance was escalated

evidence.title: Aug 2026 monthly report — SI Portal acknowledgement

rejected.title: Submit full and complete information to SEBI at the time of registration
rejected.summary: The portfolio manager must ensure that all information submitted to SEBI with its registration application is full and complete in all respects, as incomplete submissions may delay processing.

clause.excerpt: The information submitted to SEBI at the time of registration, shall be full and complete in all respects

control.name: Registration application completeness review
control.description: Before filing the registration application, a designated officer reviews the submission against SEBI's required information set and confirms every field is complete, accurate and supported by documentation; any gaps are remediated prior to submission.

evidenceSpec.description: The registration application as filed with SEBI, together with a completed pre-submission completeness checklist signed off by the responsible officer
Verification that every mandatory field in the registration submission is populated and no placeholder or blank responses remain

rejected.title: Prior intimation to SEBI before offering co-investment services
rejected.summary: A Portfolio Manager that is also the Manager of a Category I or Category II AIF must give prior intimation to SEBI before acting as a Co-investment Portfolio Manager and offering co-investment services through the portfolio management route.

clause.excerpt: A Manager of Category I or Category II Alternative Investment Fund (“AIF”) who is also a SEBI registered Portfolio Manager, and intends to act as Co-investment Portfolio Manager and offer Co-investment services through portfolio management route, shall do so only under prior intimation to SEBI.

control.name: Pre-activity SEBI intimation gate
control.description: Before commencing co-investment services through the portfolio management route, compliance verifies that the entity is a SEBI registered Portfolio Manager and the Manager of a Category I or Category II AIF, then files a prior intimation with SEBI and records it; co-investment activity is commenced only after the intimation is submitted.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the prior intimation submitted to SEBI, with submission date and proof of dispatch
SEBI acknowledgment or receipt of the intimation, if issued
Register entry confirming the intimation date precedes commencement of any co-investment activity, and that the entity holds PM registration and manages a Category I or II AIF

rejected.title: Seek SEBI registration as Portfolio Manager to offer co-investment services
rejected.summary: A Manager of a Category I or Category II AIF who is not a SEBI-registered Portfolio Manager must obtain registration as a Portfolio Manager under the PM Regulations before acting as a Co-investment Portfolio Manager and offering co-investment services through the portfolio management route.

clause.excerpt: Any other Manager of Category I or Category II AIF, who is not a SEBI registered Portfolio Manager, and intends to act as Co-investment Portfolio Manager and offer Co-investment services through portfolio management route, shall seek registration from SEBI as a Portfolio Manager in terms of the PM Regulations.

control.name: PM registration gate before co-investment launch
control.description: Before an unregistered Category I/II AIF manager commences co-investment services through the portfolio management route, a compliance checkpoint verifies whether the entity holds a SEBI Portfolio Manager registration; if not, service launch is blocked until an application for registration under the PM Regulations is filed with SEBI and registration is granted.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the application for registration as Portfolio Manager filed with SEBI under the PM Regulations
SEBI registration certificate as Portfolio Manager granted to the AIF manager

rejected.title: Obtain SEBI prior approval before offering PMS other than co-investment
rejected.summary: A Portfolio Manager registered under this route may offer portfolio management services beyond co-investment only after complying with all provisions of the PM Regulations, including eligibility criteria, and obtaining SEBI's prior approval.

clause.excerpt: Pursuant to the grant of registration, if such Portfolio Manager is desirous of offering portfolio management services other than Co-investment, the same shall be subject to compliance with all provisions of the PM Regulations including eligibility criteria, and with the prior approval of SEBI.

control.name: Pre-approval gate for expanded PMS offering
control.description: Any plan to offer portfolio management services other than co-investment is routed through a checkpoint that confirms compliance with all PM Regulations including the eligibility criteria, and that SEBI's prior approval has been obtained and recorded before such services commence.

evidenceSpec.description: SEBI prior approval permitting the Portfolio Manager to offer portfolio management services other than co-investment
Completed PM Regulations eligibility-criteria assessment evidencing compliance before launch of non-co-investment services

rejected.title: Place orders individually per client or pooled from PM account in specific situations
rejected.summary: In the specific, non-generic situations contemplated, orders must be placed for each client individually or pooled from the trading account of the Portfolio Manager, and this mode must not be applied as a generic practice.

clause.excerpt: Specific situations (not generic) wherein the orders shall be placed for each client individually or pooled from trading account of Portfolio Manager.

control.name: Order placement mode control
control.description: At order entry, classify each order against the defined specific situations and route it for each client individually or pool it from the Portfolio Manager's trading account as prescribed, ensuring the pooled route is used only in the specified situations and never generically.

evidenceSpec.description: Order audit trail evidencing that orders arising in the specified situations were placed individually per client or pooled from the Portfolio Manager's trading account as required.
Compliance-approved mapping of the specific situations to the permitted order placement mode (individual or pooled).

rejected.title: Disclose how margins/collaterals are segregated among clients
rejected.summary: Where the portfolio manager must place margins or collaterals to execute transactions, it must disclose details of how such margins/collaterals are segregated or placed from amongst various clients without affecting the interest of any client.

clause.excerpt: details on how such margins / collaterals shall be segregated / placed from amongst various clients, without affecting the interest of any client.

control.name: Margin/collateral segregation and disclosure control
control.description: Maintain a documented methodology for allocating margins/collaterals placed for executing transactions across clients, ensure the allocation does not disadvantage any client, and include this methodology in client-facing disclosures.

evidenceSpec.description: Client agreement or disclosure document page setting out how margins/collaterals are segregated or placed amongst clients
Internal policy on allocation of margins/collaterals across clients ensuring no client's interest is affected
Sample check of client disclosures confirming the margin/collateral segregation methodology was provided

rejected.title: Ensure the dealing terminal (DT) is suitably staffed
rejected.summary: Portfolio managers must maintain adequate, suitable staffing of the dealing terminal function at all times. Adequate staffing of DT is a standing condition of operating as a portfolio manager.

clause.excerpt: ensure that DT is suitably staffed

control.name: DT staffing adequacy review
control.description: Maintain an approved staffing plan for the dealing terminal, including named DT operators per shift, required qualifications, and backup coverage; periodically verify headcount and competency against the plan and escalate or fill gaps so DT is never understaffed during market hours.

evidenceSpec.description: Current DT staffing roster listing operators, shifts, and backup personnel, with approval by senior management.
Records of DT operator qualifications or certifications demonstrating suitability of staff.
Staffing-level check confirming DT operator headcount meets the approved plan for every trading session, with exceptions logged and remediated.

rejected.title: Value portfolio debt and money market securities per APMI standardized norms
rejected.summary: Portfolio managers must carry out valuation of all portfolio debt and money market securities in accordance with the standardized valuation norms prescribed by APMI, which mirror the corresponding Mutual Fund norms.

clause.excerpt: Valuation of the portfolio debt and money market securities by portfolio managers shall be carried out in accordance with these standardized valuation norms prescribed by APMI.

control.name: APMI norm-aligned securities valuation
control.description: Operate a valuation process for all debt and money market securities held in managed portfolios that applies the APMI-prescribed standardized valuation methodology (aligned to Mutual Fund norms). The valuation policy and pricing engine are mapped to the APMI norms, each security's valuation is produced by the approved methodology, and any deviation or manual override is flagged, reviewed and escalated.

evidenceSpec.description: Valuation policy document explicitly referencing the APMI standardized valuation norms and their application to portfolio debt and money market securities
Sample of valued debt and money market securities with computed prices traced back to the APMI standardized valuation methodology, showing conformity for each instrument

rejected.title: Use only APMI-empanelled valuation agencies for debt and money market securities
rejected.summary: Portfolio Managers must source valuation services for debt and money market securities in their managed portfolios exclusively from one or more valuation agencies empanelled by APMI.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall mandatorily use valuation services obtained only from one or more of such empanelled valuation agencies for the purpose of valuation of debt and money market securities in portfolios managed by them.

control.name: Empanelled-agency valuation whitelist
