control.description: Maintain an approved-vendor list restricted to APMI-empanelled valuation agencies and configure valuation workflows so that prices for debt and money market securities can be sourced only from agencies on that list, with non-empanelled vendors blocked.

evidenceSpec.description: Valuation source audit trail showing every debt and money market security price was obtained from an APMI-empanelled valuation agency
Signed service contracts or engagement letters with the empanelled valuation agencies in use

rejected.title: Retain ultimate responsibility for fair valuation of portfolio securities
rejected.summary: The Portfolio Manager remains ultimately accountable for the fair valuation of portfolio securities and cannot shift that responsibility onto the valuation agency supplying prices.

clause.excerpt: The ultimate responsibility for fair valuation shall be that of the Portfolio Manager.

control.name: Fair valuation accountability framework
control.description: Operate a valuation governance process in which the Portfolio Manager reviews and signs off on fair valuations of debt and money market securities, documenting that accountability is retained in-house even when prices are externally sourced.

evidenceSpec.description: Valuation policy or governance charter naming the Portfolio Manager as the owner of fair valuation
Periodic Portfolio Manager review and sign-off records on valuation outputs for managed portfolios

rejected.title: Track OTO/OTM RFQ trades vs total CB secondary trades on rolling 3-month basis
rejected.summary: Portfolio Managers must, to ensure compliance with the 10 percent requirement, take into account trades executed by value through the OTO or OTM mode of RFQ relative to total secondary market trades in CBs, measured over the current month plus the immediate preceding two months on a rolling basis.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall consider the trades executed by value through OTO or OTM mode of RFQ with respect to the total secondary market trades in CBs, during the current month and immediate preceding two months on a rolling basis.

control.name: Rolling 3-month OTO/OTM RFQ trade ratio monitoring
control.description: Maintain a monthly computation of the value of trades executed through OTO or OTM mode of RFQ as a proportion of total secondary market trades in CBs, using a rolling window of the current month and the two immediately preceding months, and use it to verify the 10 percent requirement is met.

evidenceSpec.description: Computation showing value of OTO/OTM RFQ trades divided by total secondary market CB trades for the rolling window of current month plus preceding two months
Monthly rolling-basis compliance report evidencing consideration of the 10 percent requirement

rejected.title: Execute both-side CB trades through RFQ in OTO mode
rejected.summary: Every corporate bond transaction in which the Portfolio Manager is on both sides of the trade must be executed on the RFQ platform in OTO mode. Transactions initiated in OTM mode that are executed with another Portfolio Manager count as OTM mode and fall outside this OTO requirement.

clause.excerpt: All transactions in CBs wherein Portfolio Managers is on both sides of the trade shall be executed through RFQ in OTO mode.

control.name: OTO-mode RFQ routing check
control.description: Operate an order-routing validation that identifies any CB transaction where the Portfolio Manager is on both sides of the trade and permits execution only through the RFQ platform in OTO mode, while recording OTM-mode transactions executed with another Portfolio Manager as OTM.

evidenceSpec.description: RFQ platform trade log extract showing each CB transaction with both-side PM exposure tagged with its execution mode (OTO or OTM)
Trade confirmations or exchange trade files evidencing that both-side CB transactions were executed in OTO mode on the RFQ platform

rejected.title: Ensure at least 10% of CB secondary market trades executed via RFQ OTO/OTM mode
rejected.summary: Portfolio Managers must ensure that at least 10% by value of their secondary market trades in CBs, measured over the current month and the immediate preceding two months, are executed by placing or seeking quotes through the OTO or OTM mode of RFQ. The rolling three-month window is used for computing the percentage.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall ensure that at least 10% (by value) of their secondary market trades in CBs in current month and immediate preceding two months are executed by placing / seeking quotes through OTO or OTM mode of RFQ.

control.name: RFQ execution threshold monitoring
control.description: Track all secondary market trades in CBs on a rolling three-month basis (current month plus immediate preceding two months), tag trades executed through the OTO or OTM mode of RFQ, compute their share by value of total CB secondary market trades, and escalate corrective action if the share falls below 10%.

evidenceSpec.description: Monthly computation showing value of secondary market CB trades executed via OTO/OTM RFQ mode divided by total value of secondary market CB trades over the current month and immediate preceding two months, confirming the ratio is at least 10%.
Trade-level extract of secondary market CB transactions for the rolling three-month window, with RFQ mode (OTO/OTM) tags, reconciled to the order/trade management system.

rejected.title: Appoint SEBI registered Custodians before dealing in ETCDs
rejected.summary: A Portfolio Manager must appoint a custodian registered with SEBI before it undertakes any dealing in Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives. Dealing in such derivatives is not permitted until a SEBI registered custodian has been appointed.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall appoint SEBI registered Custodians before dealing in Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives.

control.name: Custodian appointment gate for ETCD dealing
control.description: Maintain a pre-trade control that blocks any Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives transaction until the firm has formally appointed a custodian holding valid SEBI registration. Verify the custodian's SEBI registration at appointment, execute the custodial agreement, record the appointment date, and re-verify registration status before continuing ETCD dealing if the appointment lapses.

evidenceSpec.description: Executed custodian appointment letter or custodial agreement with the SEBI registered custodian, together with the custodian's SEBI registration certificate or registration number
Report comparing the custodian appointment date against the firm's ETCD trade records confirming that no Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives transaction predates the appointment

rejected.title: Ensure ETCD participation for clients complies with applicable rules and position limits
rejected.summary: A Portfolio Manager trading Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives on behalf of clients must ensure that such participation complies with all rules, regulations (including the PM Regulations), circulars/guidelines and position limit norms applicable to clients, as issued by SEBI and recognized stock exchanges.

clause.excerpt: such participation shall be in compliance with all the rules, regulations including the PM Regulations and circulars/guidelines and position limit norms as may be applicable to

control.name: ETCD client-side compliance check
control.description: Before and while placing Exchange Traded Commodity Derivative orders on behalf of each client, verify that the trade and resulting positions conform to the PM Regulations, SEBI and stock exchange circulars/guidelines, and the position limit norms applicable to clients; block, reduce or unwind any trade that would breach these limits.

evidenceSpec.description: Client-level ETCD position monitoring report showing each client's open positions against the position limit norms applicable to clients, with breaches flagged and resolved
Compliance checklist mapping the PM Regulations and current SEBI and recognized stock exchange circulars and guidelines to the ETCD trades executed for clients

rejected.title: Dispose of physical commodities received via delivery within agreed timelines
rejected.summary: Where commodity derivatives dealings result in the Portfolio Manager holding physical goods, the Portfolio Manager must dispose of them at the earliest, within timelines agreed with the client, and bears responsibility for liquidating them.

clause.excerpt: the goods need to be disposed off at the earliest, within the timelines as agreed upon between the client and the Portfolio Manager. The responsibility of liquidating the physical goods shall be with the Portfolio Manager.

control.name: Physical commodity disposal monitoring
control.description: Maintain a register of physical commodities received on delivery and track disposal against client-agreed timelines, escalating any position approaching the agreed deadline.

evidenceSpec.description: Log of physical commodity holdings with delivery dates, client-agreed disposal timelines, and completed disposal records

rejected.title: Ensure FPI clients meet all SEBI conditions for ETCD participation
rejected.summary: When onboarding Foreign Portfolio Investors as clients and when executing Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives transactions for them, Portfolio Managers must ensure compliance with every condition specified by SEBI for FPI participation in that market.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall, while onboarding FPIs as clients and executing transactions in Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives market, ensure that all conditions specified by SEBI are complied with.

control.name: FPI onboarding and ETCD transaction compliance check
control.description: Before an FPI is accepted as a client and before any Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives transaction is executed for an FPI, the firm runs a checklist validating that the client and the proposed trade satisfy each SEBI-specified condition for FPI participation in the ETCD market; non-compliant onboarding or orders are blocked and escalated.

evidenceSpec.description: FPI onboarding checklist or clearance record showing each SEBI-specified condition was verified before the client was accepted.
Trade-level check confirming every ETCD transaction executed for FPI clients was tagged to a compliant, condition-verified FPI account.

rejected.title: Periodic client reports on Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives exposure
rejected.summary: Portfolio Managers must provide clients with periodic reports, prepared as per the PM Regulations, covering the clients' exposure in Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall also provide periodic reports to the clients as per the PM Regulations regarding their exposure in Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives.

control.name: Periodic ETCD client reporting
control.description: Operate a recurring reporting cycle that computes each client's exposure in Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives, formats the report in line with the PM Regulations, and dispatches it to the client at the prescribed periodicity.

evidenceSpec.description: Copies of the periodic client reports issued, showing each client's Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives exposure as per the PM Regulations.
Check that every client due a report in the period received one, and that the reported ETCD exposure figures reconcile to the client's derivative positions.

rejected.title: Report ETCD exposure under 'Commodity Derivatives' heading in monthly SEBI reports
rejected.summary: Portfolio Managers must include their exposure in Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives under the 'Commodity Derivatives' heading in the monthly reports they submit to SEBI.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall report the exposure in Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives under the heading of ‘Commodity Derivatives’ in the monthly reports submitted to SEBI.

control.name: Monthly ETCD exposure reporting control

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the monthly report submitted to SEBI showing Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives exposure under the 'Commodity Derivatives' heading, with submission timestamp.
Reconciliation of the reported ETCD exposure figure against the underlying position/exposure records for the reporting month.

rejected.title: Obtain prior client consent before investing in related party or associate securities
rejected.summary: Regulation 22(1A) of the PM Regulations provides that a Portfolio Manager may invest in securities of its related parties or associates only after obtaining the client's prior consent, in the manner specified by the Board. Reconciliation of executed related-party/associate securities trades against the consent register, confirming no trade was executed without prior client consent.

rejected.title: Obtain client consent for associate/related party investments at onboarding
rejected.summary: When onboarding new clients, the Portfolio Manager must secure the client's prior consent before making any investments in securities of the Portfolio Manager's associates or related parties.

control.name: Onboarding consent gate

evidenceSpec.description: Signed onboarding form or consent record per client showing consent for investments in associates'/related parties' securities
Report of new clients onboarded in the period cross-checked against consent records, flagging any associate/related party investment made without consent

rejected.title: No investment in below investment grade listed securities
rejected.summary: Portfolio Managers offering non-discretionary portfolio management services must not invest client assets in listed securities rated below investment grade. This is a standing prohibition on all such investments.

control.description: Maintain a rating-based restriction list and block any purchase of listed securities rated below investment grade in non-discretionary client portfolios, with periodic re-verification of existing holdings against current ratings.

evidenceSpec.description: Pre-trade compliance check log showing orders in below investment grade listed securities are rejected for non-discretionary portfolios
Holdings report evidencing zero exposure to listed securities rated below investment grade across non-discretionary client portfolios

rejected.title: Limit unlisted unrated investments to 10% of client AUM, excluding related parties
rejected.summary: If the Portfolio Manager chooses to invest non-discretionary client assets in unlisted unrated securities, such investments must not exceed 10% of the client's assets under management and must not be in issuers that are associates or related parties of the Portfolio Manager.

control.name: Unlisted unrated exposure cap monitor

evidenceSpec.description: Report showing unlisted unrated holdings as a percentage of each non-discretionary client's AUM, all within 10%
Associates/related parties register with screening records evidencing no unlisted unrated holdings in issuers related to the Portfolio Manager

rejected.title: Keep unlisted unrated debt and hybrid securities within 25% unlisted limit
rejected.summary: Any unlisted unrated debt and hybrid securities held for non-discretionary clients must remain within the overall 25% cap for investment in unlisted securities prescribed by Regulation 24(4) of the PM Regulations.

control.name: Regulation 24(4) unlisted limit check

evidenceSpec.description: Compliance report showing total unlisted securities exposure, including unlisted unrated debt and hybrid securities, within the 25% limit under Regulation 24(4)
Compliance officer certificate confirming adherence to the Regulation 24(4) unlisted securities limit

rejected.title: Disclose conflicts of interest for associate/related-party securities to advisory clients
rejected.summary: For advisory portfolio management services, the portfolio manager must make suitable disclosure to the client about conflicts of interest arising from investments in the securities of associates/related parties at the time advice is given.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall make suitable disclosure to the client regarding conflict of interest with respect to investments in the securities of the associates/related parties, while giving advice

control.name: Conflict-of-interest disclosure at point of advice
control.description: Before or while rendering advice to an advisory portfolio management client, disclose to that client any conflict of interest concerning investments in securities of associates or related parties, applying the definition of 'associate' from the explanation to Regulation 24(3C) of the PM Regulations.

evidenceSpec.description: Sample of client advice records or disclosure statements evidencing the conflict-of-interest disclosure made to advisory clients
Register mapping advised securities to associate/related-party issuers, with disclosure status flagged for each advice event

rejected.title: Disclose credit rating of all securities while giving advice
rejected.summary: When giving advice under advisory portfolio management services, the portfolio manager must disclose the credit rating of all securities covered by the advice.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall disclose the credit rating of all securities, while giving advice

control.name: Credit-rating disclosure at point of advice
control.description: Ensure that every advice communication to advisory clients includes the credit rating of each security being advised upon, sourced from a current ratings feed.

evidenceSpec.description: Sample of client advice or communication records showing the credit rating disclosed for each advised security
Validation that advice records carry a populated credit-rating field for all advised securities

rejected.title: Standard ToR must cover clients' portfolios under all services for performance audit
rejected.summary: The standard Terms of Reference for the audit of firm-level performance data must expressly require that clients' portfolios under all services are considered in the audit.

clause.excerpt: The standard ToR shall inter-alia include requirement for Portfolio Managers to consider clients’ portfolios under all services for the purpose of audit of firm-level performance data.

control.name: Standard ToR content review
control.description: Compliance reviews the standard Terms of Reference used for the audit of firm-level performance data and confirms it contains the requirement that clients' portfolios under all services are considered; the ToR is re-checked whenever it is revised or a new audit is commissioned.

evidenceSpec.description: Current standard Terms of Reference for the firm-level performance data audit showing the clause requiring consideration of clients' portfolios under all services
Compliance review log recording that the ToR version used for each performance data audit contains the all-services portfolio coverage requirement

rejected.title: Apply paragraphs 5.6.1 to 5.6.6 to all performance reporting and advertising
rejected.summary: Any entity that reports, publishes or advertises the performance of any Investment Approach of a Portfolio Manager must comply with the requirements set out in paragraphs 5.6.1 to 5.6.6.

control.name: Performance communication compliance gate

evidenceSpec.description: Register of all performance reports, publications and advertisements for Investment Approaches, each bearing dated pre-release compliance sign-off against the requirements of paragraphs 5.6.1 to 5.6.6.
Periodic scan of the firm's websites, portals and public communication channels for Investment Approach performance claims, confirming each was captured in the pre-release compliance gate.

rejected.title: Strictly comply with the aforesaid Regulation
rejected.summary: Portfolio managers must ensure full and strict compliance with the referenced Regulation at all times.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio managers shall strictly comply with the aforesaid Regulation.

control.name: Regulatory compliance monitoring
control.description: Maintain a compliance register mapping the requirements of the referenced Regulation to the firm's operations, monitor ongoing adherence, and escalate any deviations or breaches for remediation.

evidenceSpec.description: Signed periodic compliance certificate/attestation confirming adherence to the aforesaid Regulation
Breach and exception register showing no instances of non-compliance with the aforesaid Regulation, or logged remediation of any found

rejected.title: Submit certificate application in Form A with non-refundable fee
rejected.summary: A person seeking grant of a certificate must apply to the Board using Form A of Schedule I, and the application must be accompanied by the prescribed non-refundable application fee.

clause.excerpt: An application by a person for the grant of a certificate shall be made to the Board in Form A of Schedule I and shall be accompanied by a non-refundable application fee, as specified in para (1) of Schedule II.

control.name: Registration application assembly and submission control
control.description: Maintain a checklist-driven process that compiles the complete Form A application per Schedule I, arranges payment of the non-refundable application fee per Schedule II, verifies completeness of enclosures, and submits the application to the Board, recording the submission date and acknowledgement.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the completed Form A application as submitted to the Board
Proof of payment of the non-refundable application fee (fee receipt or bank instrument)
Board acknowledgement of receipt confirming the application was filed with fee paid

rejected.title: Remove objections indicated by the Board within 3 weeks
rejected.summary: When the Board indicates objections to a registration application, the applicant must be given, and must use, the opportunity to remove those objections within the time specified, which cannot exceed 3 weeks, failing which the incomplete application is rejected.

clause.excerpt: Provided that, before rejecting any such application, the applicant shall be given an opportunity to remove objections indicated by the Board, within the time specified, not later than 3 weeks.

control.name: Board objection remediation tracker
control.description: On receipt of a communication from the Board indicating objections to the application, log the objections, assign an owner, prepare and submit the rectification to the Board within the time specified (not later than 3 weeks from the Board's communication), and track the response until the application is accepted so it is not rejected as incomplete.

evidenceSpec.description: Board communication (letter or email) listing the objections indicated and the time specified for their removal
Rectification submission filed with the Board removing the indicated objections, with submission date visible
Date-difference check confirming the removal submission was made within 21 days (3 weeks) of the Board's objection communication

rejected.title: Appear before the Board for personal representation when required
rejected.summary: The applicant or its principal officer must appear before the SEBI Board for personal representation if the Board so requires.

clause.excerpt: The applicant or its principal officer shall, if so required, appear before the Board for personal representation.

evidenceSpec.description: Board notice requesting personal representation together with confirmation of appearance (attendance record or minutes) for the applicant or principal officer

rejected.title: Appoint a compliance officer
rejected.summary: The applicant must have appointed a compliance officer, which the Board verifies as one of the conditions for grant of registration.

clause.excerpt: the applicant has appointed a compliance officer

control.name: Compliance officer appointment and continuity

evidenceSpec.description: Appointment letter or board resolution designating the compliance officer

rejected.title: Raise net worth to five crore rupees within 36 months of 2020 Regulations commencement
rejected.summary: Portfolio managers holding a certificate of registration before the commencement of the SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020 must raise their net worth to at least five crore rupees within thirty-six months of that commencement.

rejected.title: Pay registration fees in the prescribed manner
rejected.summary: The portfolio manager must pay the fees for registration as provided in the regulations.

clause.excerpt: the portfolio manager shall pay the fees for registration in the manner provided in these regulations

control.name: Registration fee payment
control.description: Finance process to compute and remit registration fees through the prescribed channel and record the payment against the registration file.

evidenceSpec.description: Fee payment challan or confirmation evidencing payment of registration fees

rejected.title: Maintain net worth specified in regulation 9 at all times
rejected.summary: The portfolio manager must maintain the net worth prescribed in regulation 9 at all times during the period of the certificate (the clause exempts Co-investment Portfolio Managers from this condition).

clause.excerpt: the portfolio manager shall maintain the net worth specified in regulation 9 at all times during the period of the certificate

control.name: Net worth monitoring
control.description: Periodic computation of net worth per regulation 9 with supporting certificates, breach alerts and escalation and restoration plans if net worth falls below the prescribed level.

evidenceSpec.description: Net worth computation showing net worth at or above the regulation 9 level at each monitoring date
Chartered accountant or auditor certificate of net worth

rejected.title: Pay certificate fees within 15 days of Board intimation
rejected.summary: An applicant eligible for grant of a certificate must pay the prescribed fees within 15 days of receiving intimation from the Board, in the manner specified in Schedule II. clause.excerpt: shall pay such fees within 15 days of receiving intimation from the Board and in such manner as specified in Schedule II

Ledger or bank record confirming the fee payment date falls within 15 days of the Board intimation date

rejected.title: Abide by the provisions of the Act and these regulations
rejected.summary: As a condition of the certificate of registration, the portfolio manager must comply with the provisions of the Act and the portfolio manager regulations.

clause.excerpt: the portfolio manager shall abide by the provisions of the Act and these regulations

control.name: Regulatory compliance register

evidenceSpec.description: Compliance register or calendar mapping Act and regulation provisions to responsible owners and review dates
Periodic compliance attestation signed by the compliance officer confirming adherence

rejected.title: Obtain prior Board approval for change in control
rejected.summary: Any change in control of the portfolio manager requires prior approval of the SEBI Board, obtained in the manner the Board specifies, before the change takes effect.

evidenceSpec.description: SEBI prior approval letter for the change in control
Shareholding and control register reconciled against SEBI approval records before executing any transfer

rejected.title: Forthwith inform Board of false or materially changed information
rejected.summary: If information or particulars previously submitted to the Board are found to be false or misleading in any material particular, or if there is any material change in information already submitted, the portfolio manager must inform the Board in writing forthwith.

control.name: Submitted-information change monitor

Change log of submitted particulars with detection dates and Board intimation references

rejected.title: Pay registration fees in the manner provided in the regulations
rejected.summary: The portfolio manager must pay the fees for registration in the manner provided in the regulations as a condition of the certificate.

clause.excerpt: the portfolio manager shall pay the fees for registration in the manner provided in these regulations

rejected.title: Redress investor grievances within 21 days and report complaints to Board

Complaint statistics (number, nature and particulars) submitted to the Board

rejected.title: Maintain the prescribed net worth at all times
rejected.summary: The portfolio manager must maintain the net worth specified in regulation 9 at all times while the certificate of registration is in force; the requirement does not apply to a Co-investment Portfolio Manager.

rejected.title: Cease all portfolio management activity upon refusal of certificate

rejected.title: Obtain prior client consent before investing in related party or associate securities
rejected.summary: The portfolio manager may invest in securities of its related parties or associates only after obtaining the client's prior consent, in such manner as the Board may specify from time to time.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager may make investments in the securities of its related parties or its associates only after obtaining the prior consent of the client in such manner as may be specified by the Board from time to time

control.name: Prior consent gate for related-party investments
control.description: Orders to buy or sell securities of the portfolio manager's related parties or associates are blocked in the order management system unless a dated, recorded prior client consent exists in the manner specified by the Board; compliance periodically reviews the mapping of such trades to consents.

evidenceSpec.description: Log of all executed investments in related party or associate securities, each mapped to a client consent record dated before trade execution
Client consent records captured in the manner specified by the Board

rejected.title: Include prescribed contents in client agreement
rejected.summary: Every agreement between the portfolio manager and the client must include the mandated items: investment objectives and services, contract period and early termination, investment approach and client restrictions, instruments and exposure proportions, tenure, early withdrawal terms, attendant risks, investment amount, settlement procedure, fees, custody, the discretionary liability cap, accounting/audit/reporting terms, and other regulatory-compliant terms.

clause.excerpt: The agreement between the portfolio manager and the client shall, inter alia, include the following

control.name: Client agreement template gate
control.description: Maintain a master client agreement template covering every mandated clause; compliance reviews and approves the template and each executed agreement to confirm all required contents are present before signing.

evidenceSpec.description: Executed client agreement evidencing inclusion of all prescribed clauses, including the discretionary portfolio manager liability cap where applicable

rejected.title: Co-investment terms not more favourable than AIF terms
rejected.summary: For a Co-investment Portfolio Manager, the agreement terms for co-investment in an investee company by a co-investor must not be more favourable than the terms of investment of the Alternative Investment Fund.

clause.excerpt: the terms of co-investment in an investee company by a co-investor, shall not be more favourable than the terms of investment of the Alternative Investment Fund

control.name: Co-investment parity review
control.description: Before executing co-investment documents, compare each term offered to the co-investor with the corresponding term of the AIF's investment in the investee company and confirm no term is more favourable to the co-investor.

evidenceSpec.description: Co-investment termsheet or agreement with a documented parity comparison sign-off against the AIF's investment terms

rejected.title: Co-investment exit terms identical to AIF exit terms
rejected.summary: For a Co-investment Portfolio Manager, the exit terms from co-investment in an investee company, including the timing of exit, must be identical to the exit terms applicable to the Alternative Investment Fund.

clause.excerpt: the terms of exit from the Co-investment in an investee company including the timing of exit shall be identical to the terms applicable to that of exit of the Alternative Investment Fund

control.name: Exit mirroring check
control.description: At the time of exit from an investee company, apply the identical exit terms and timing to the co-investor as those applicable to the AIF's exit and record the alignment before executing the exit.

evidenceSpec.description: Exit documentation evidencing identical terms and timing of exit for the AIF and the co-investor in the investee company

rejected.title: Allow co-investor early withdrawal only to extent of AIF exit
rejected.summary: For a Co-investment Portfolio Manager, early withdrawal of funds by co-investors from co-investment in investee companies is permitted only to the extent the Alternative Investment Fund has also exited from its respective investment in those companies.

clause.excerpt: the early withdrawal of funds by the co-investors with respect to Co-investment in investee companies shall be allowed to the extent that the Alternative Investment Fund has also made an exit from respective investment in such investee companies

control.name: Early withdrawal gate
control.description: Before processing any co-investor early withdrawal request, verify the extent of the AIF's exit from the relevant investee company and permit the withdrawal only up to that exited extent.

evidenceSpec.description: Withdrawal processing log matching each co-investor early withdrawal amount against the AIF's exited extent in the same investee company

rejected.title: Disclose related-party investments and diversification policy
rejected.summary: The Disclosure Document must include details of the investment of client's funds by the portfolio manager in securities of its related parties or associates, and the details of the portfolio manager's diversification policy. The Board may exempt specified portfolio managers from these two disclosures.

clause.excerpt: (da) the details of investment of client’s funds by the portfolio manager in the securities of its related parties or associates; (db) the details of diversification policy of the portfolio manager:

control.name: Related-party investment and diversification disclosure check
control.description: Track investments of client funds in securities of related parties or associates and formally document the diversification policy; verify both sets of details are included in the Disclosure Document, applying any Board-specified exemption where relevant.

evidenceSpec.description: Disclosure Document section detailing investments of client funds in related-party or associate securities and the diversification policy

rejected.title: File copy of Disclosure Document with the Board before circulating it to any client
rejected.summary: After the certificate of registration is granted, the portfolio manager must file a copy of the Disclosure Document with the Board before circulating it to any client.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall file with the Board, a copy of the Disclosure Document after grant of certificate of registration before circulating it to any client

control.name: Disclosure Document pre-circulation filing gate
control.description: A release gate that prevents circulation of the Disclosure Document to any client until a copy has been filed with the Board following grant of the certificate of registration, with the filing acknowledgement recorded against the document version.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the Disclosure Document as filed with the Board, together with the SEBI filing or submission acknowledgement
Log showing the Board filing date precedes the earliest date the Disclosure Document was circulated to any client

rejected.title: Non-discretionary PM to manage funds per client directions
rejected.summary: A non-discretionary portfolio manager must manage client funds strictly in accordance with the directions issued by the client.

clause.excerpt: the non-discretionary portfolio manager shall manage the funds in accordance with the directions of the client

control.name: Client instruction adherence check
control.description: Record each client's directions before execution and reconcile executed transactions against those directions, escalating any trade that deviates from the client's instruction.

evidenceSpec.description: Reconciliation of executed transactions against recorded client directions
Signed client direction letters or instruction logs retained as proof of adherence

rejected.title: Segregate each client's securities holdings in separate accounts
rejected.summary: The portfolio manager must keep each client's holdings in securities in separate accounts, so that one client's securities are not held together with another client's.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall segregate each client’s holding in securities in separate accounts.

control.name: Client-wise securities account segregation
control.description: Maintain a distinct securities account for each client, ensure all purchases and holdings of securities are recorded in the respective client's own account, and periodically verify that no client's securities are commingled with the portfolio manager's own holdings or with another client's holdings.

evidenceSpec.description: Client-wise securities account statements or ledger extracts showing each client's holdings held in a separate account
Reconciliation check confirming a one-to-one mapping of clients to securities accounts with no cross-client commingling

rejected.title: Proper and timely handling of client complaints
rejected.summary: The portfolio manager must ensure that complaints received from clients are handled properly and in a timely manner, and take appropriate action immediately.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall ensure proper and timely handling of complaints from his clients and take appropriate action immediately.

control.name: Client complaint handling process
control.description: Maintain a complaint management workflow in which every client complaint is logged on receipt, assigned for resolution, actioned promptly and tracked through to closure with timestamps at each step.

evidenceSpec.description: Complaint register or CRM log showing complaints received from clients, the actions taken and the dates of receipt and action.
Check that every logged client complaint has a recorded action taken immediately and a closure status.

rejected.title: Ensure compliance with Board-specified prudential investment limits
rejected.summary: The portfolio manager must ensure client investments comply with prudential limits specified by the Board, which apply at the individual client level at the time each investment is made.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall ensure compliance with the prudential limits on investments as may be specified by the Board.

control.name: Prudential limit pre-trade check
control.description: At the time of making each investment, test the proposed position against the Board-specified prudential limits computed at the individual client level; reject or resize trades that would breach a limit.

evidenceSpec.description: Client-level position report showing each client's exposure measured against the applicable prudential limits at the time of each investment
Prudential limit compliance policy and periodic breach exception log

rejected.title: No investment in unrated securities of related parties or associates
rejected.summary: The portfolio manager must not invest client funds in unrated securities issued by its related parties or its associates (bodies corporate meeting the twenty percent cross-holding tests).

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall not be allowed to invest clients’ funds in unrated securities of their related parties or their associates.

control.name: Related-party unrated securities block
control.description: Maintain a register of related parties and associates determined via the twenty percent paid-up equity/partnership interest tests, and screen every proposed investment to block unrated securities issued by any entity on that register.

evidenceSpec.description: Register of related parties and associates with the twenty percent shareholding computations supporting each designation
Screening log of client investments confirming no unrated related-party or associate securities are held

rejected.title: Invest client funds based on Board-specified credit ratings
rejected.summary: The portfolio manager must ensure that client funds are invested on the basis of the credit ratings of securities as specified by the Board.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall ensure investment of its clients’ funds on the basis of the credit rating of securities as may be specified by the Board

control.name: Credit-rating based investment check
control.description: Before investing client funds in a rated instrument class, verify the security carries a credit rating meeting the Board-specified rating criteria; record the rating relied upon for each investment decision.

evidenceSpec.description: Report of client investments mapped to the credit ratings of the securities, showing ratings meet Board-specified criteria
Credit rating assessment policy and investment decision records citing the rating basis for each purchase

rejected.title: Co-investment Portfolio Manager to invest 100% of AUM in specified unlisted securities
rejected.summary: A Co-investment Portfolio Manager must invest the entire assets under management of the co-investment portfolio in unlisted securities of investee companies in which Category I or Category II Alternative Investment Funds managed by it as Manager have invested.

clause.excerpt: The Co-investment Portfolio Manager shall invest hundred percent of the assets under management in unlisted securities of investee companies where Category I and Category II Alternative Investment Funds managed by it as Manager, make investment;

control.name: Co-investment portfolio composition check
control.description: Before and after each co-investment, verify that every holding of the co-investment portfolio is in unlisted securities of an investee company in which a Category I or Category II AIF managed by the firm as Manager has invested, so that 100% of assets under management remain allocated to such securities at all times.

evidenceSpec.description: Portfolio composition report for the co-investment portfolio evidencing that hundred percent of assets under management are held in unlisted securities

Investee-company mapping linking each co-investment to an investment made by a Category I or Category II AIF managed by the portfolio manager as Manager, such as AIF investment records or investee company registers

rejected.title: Segregate each client's funds and portfolio of securities from own funds and securities
rejected.summary: The portfolio manager must keep each client's funds and portfolio of securities separate from its own funds and securities at all times.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall segregate each clients' funds and portfolio of securities and keep them separately from his own funds and securities

control.name: Client funds and securities segregation
control.description: Maintain dedicated client bank and demat accounts separate from the portfolio manager's proprietary accounts, with client-wise segregation of funds and securities and periodic checks that no commingling with own funds or securities occurs.

evidenceSpec.description: Written segregation policy and client-wise bank/demat account mapping showing client funds and securities held separately from proprietary accounts
Reconciliation report confirming no commingling between client accounts and the portfolio manager's own funds and securities

rejected.title: Be responsible for safekeeping of clients' funds and securities
rejected.summary: The portfolio manager bears responsibility for the safekeeping of the funds and securities of its clients.

clause.excerpt: be responsible for safekeeping of clients' funds and securities

control.name: Safekeeping accountability for client assets
control.description: Operate custody, record-keeping and reconciliation processes over client funds and securities, with named accountability for safeguarding client assets and escalation of any loss or discrepancy.

evidenceSpec.description: Periodic reconciliation of client funds and securities holdings against custodian, bank and depository records evidencing safekeeping
Safekeeping and custody records, including discrepancy or incident logs for client funds and securities

rejected.title: Furnish periodic report to client at intervals not exceeding three months
rejected.summary: The portfolio manager must give each client a report at the periodicity agreed in the contract, capped at three months, covering portfolio composition and value, transactions, beneficial interest, expenses, risks, defaults in underlying debt securities and distributor commissions.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall furnish periodically a report to the client, as agreed in the contract, but not exceeding a period of three months

control.name: Periodic client reporting
control.description: A reporting cycle that generates and delivers each client's report within the contractual periodicity (never exceeding three months), ensuring the report includes portfolio composition and value, description and number of securities, goods and cash balances, aggregate portfolio value, transactions with dates and purchase/sale details, beneficial interest received, expenses incurred, risks foreseen and in recommended securities, defaults or downgrades to default rating in underlying debt securities, and commission paid to distributors for that client.

evidenceSpec.description: Client report for the reporting period containing all prescribed sections: portfolio composition and value, transactions, beneficial interest, expenses, risks, debt-security defaults/downgrades and distributor commissions
Report-delivery log evidencing that every client received a report within the agreed periodicity not exceeding three months

rejected.title: Furnish report to client as and when required by the client
rejected.summary: In addition to the periodic reporting cycle, the portfolio manager must provide the report to the client whenever the client requires it.

clause.excerpt: and as and when required by the client

control.name: On-demand client reporting
control.description: A workflow that logs client requests for reports and triggers preparation and delivery of the report with the prescribed details upon each client request.

evidenceSpec.description: Report furnished in response to a client request, containing the prescribed portfolio details
Client-request log pairing each received request with the report delivered in response

rejected.title: Appoint a compliance officer for compliance monitoring and grievance redressal
rejected.summary: Every portfolio manager must appoint a compliance officer responsible for monitoring compliance with the Act, rules, regulations and other SEBI issuances and for redressal of investors' grievances. The role cannot be assigned to the principal officer or the clause (e) employee, except that a Co-investment Portfolio Manager may assign it to the principal officer.

clause.excerpt: Every portfolio manager shall appoint a compliance officer who shall be responsible for monitoring the compliance of the Act, rules and regulations, notifications, guidelines, instructions etc., issued by the Board or the Central Government and for redressal of investors' grievances

control.name: Compliance officer appointment and segregation
control.description: Designate a named compliance officer through an internal resolution or appointment letter, ensuring the designated person is not the principal officer or the employee referred to in clause (e) of sub-regulation (2) of regulation 7 (unless the entity is a Co-investment Portfolio Manager), and formally vest the officer with responsibility for monitoring regulatory compliance and redressing investors' grievances.

evidenceSpec.description: Signed appointment letter or resolution designating the compliance officer, together with the officer's acceptance of the role and its compliance-monitoring and grievance-redressal responsibilities

Record check confirming the designated compliance officer is distinct from the principal officer and the clause (e) employee, with an exception flag where the entity is a Co-investment Portfolio Manager

rejected.title: Redress investor grievances within twenty-one calendar days
rejected.summary: The Portfolio Manager must resolve investor grievances promptly, and in any case no later than twenty-one calendar days from the date of receipt, in the manner specified by the Board.

clause.excerpt: shall redress investor grievances promptly but not later than twenty-one calendar days from the date of receipt of the grievance

control.name: Grievance receipt-to-resolution tracking
control.description: Maintain a grievance register that logs the date of receipt of each investor grievance, tracks its progress against a 21-calendar-day clock with escalation for items approaching the limit, and records the resolution taken in the manner specified by the Board.

evidenceSpec.description: Grievance register or tracker showing, for each grievance, the receipt date, resolution date and elapsed calendar days, confirming closure within 21 days
Board-specified grievance redressal procedure or policy adopted by the Portfolio Manager
